outcome: acquisition of a mature anaerobic microbiota

colonization rates and population counts of different gut bacteria (Escherichia coli, bifidobacteria, facultative bacteria, Clostridioides difficile, Staphylococcus aureus, Bacteroides, enterobacteria)
cohort: A cohort of 65 infants (FARMFLORA cohort) whose feces were collected regularly from 3 days to 18 months of age.
finding: Birth order, delivery mode, and antibiotic exposure were each independently associated with gut colonization, with firstborn infants acquiring Escherichia coli and bifidobacteria later and showing signs of microbiota immaturity.
mod_finding: Cesarean-delivered infants showed delayed E. coli acquisition and increased colonization by other enterobacteria.
